next_step: Legal to sign SLA addendum + finalize reserved GPU SKU and maintenance window
notes:
Account background:
- Established defense-adjacent analytics firm; high-sensitivity data, strict residency and audit needs.
- Initially self-hosting models, evaluating move to managed Dedicated + private control plane for faster scale.
Timeline (recent):
- 2026-01-28: Intro call (Maya/Carlos) — discovered core use: real-time threat scoring + analyst chat.
- 2026-02-14: Technical deep dive (SE-led) — Carlos demoed batching/kv-cache benefits; asked for 95th/99th token latency profiles. ff_2026-02-14_zenith-intro
- 2026-02-21: Sizing workshop — preliminary reserved GPU plan: 8xA100-equivalent nodes to hit 2k QPS across reranking + chat spikes.
- 2026-03-02: SLA negotiation meeting — discussed uptime targets, credit schedules, maintenance windows. ff_2026-03-02_sla-deep-dive
- 2026-03-08: Legal kick-off: vendor terms, data residency addendum sent to Zenith legal.
Use-case and technical requirements summary:
- Primary workloads: reranking for search results (high QPS bursts), real-time chat for analysts (low latency interactive SLOs), nightly batch summarization jobs.
- Latency targets: 95th token latency < 120ms for chat baseline, 99th < 250ms on dedicated pool; tailing rules during peak.
- Throughput / reserved GPU planning: baseline 2k QPS aggregated; target 3x headroom for spikes, plan = 8 reserved GPUs (customer's HW team asked for equivalent spec and thermal budget).
- Quality/fallbacks: must support automated fallback to smaller quantized variants for degradation; routing policy needs region-aware failover.
SLA discussion points (negotiation notes):
- Uptime: Zenith pushed for 99.95% for Dedicated control plane & inference runtime; Redwood proposed 99.9% with credit schedule tiers.
- Credit schedule proposed by Redwood: 5% service credit for monthly uptime 99.0-99.5, 15% for 98.0-99.0, 30% <98.0. Zenith countered asking steeper credits for mission-critical services.
- Maintenance windows: Zenith needs quarterly maintenance windows with 48‑hour advance notice and explicit blackout windows for their APAC customers; requesting maintenance limited to 02:00-06:00 local.
- Support SLAs: 1-hour P1 response commitment during business-critical incidents, 4-hour on-site escalation path for on-prem hardware (third-party), 24/7 pager for security incidents.
- Data controls: explicit KMS/HSM integration, per-customer audit logs with 7-year retention option.
Open technical trade-offs called out:
- Batching vs latency: Redwood recommended dynamic batching with strict per-route latency caps; Zenith skeptical for analyst chat — requested a canary where chat routes bypass batching under 75ms SLO.
- KV caching: large prefix reuse on reranking flow would reduce tokens by ~30% — need eviction policies documented in runbook.
- Quantization: Zenith's model team wants 8-bit quantized fallback but requires validated QA tests for hallucination/regression risk.
Commercial / procurement notes:
- Anchor term: 24-month reserved capacity with quarterly review; possible uplift to 36 months after successful Q2 POC.
- Pricing ask: committed discount on per-token + flat monthly reserved capacity. Estimated ARR range above.
Risks & blockers (CRM shorthand):
- Legal seeking higher credit % + SLA for control plane GCs.
- Internal hardware team has not signed off on rack power/cooling for on-prem nodes.
- Procurement timeline: budget window closes end-May; pushing to close by 2026-05.
Next steps (short):
- Redwood to produce redlined SLA with alternate credit schedule and a maintenance blackout addendum (due 2026-03-15).
- SE to deliver final reserved GPU SKU + thermal/power spec sheet to Zenith infra team (due 2026-03-20).
- Schedule joint tabletop DR exercise for maintenance fallback (target Apr).
Stitch/links: Jira tickets INF-4123/INF-4189 track infra sizing + SLA redlines.
Sales signal: High — exec sponsor engaged, procurement allocated subject to legal.
Quoted from CTO (call 2026-03-02): "If we can't get firm uptime + a sensible credit schedule, we can't move mission-critical workloads."
CRM notes style: short, actionable, some repetition expected.
